etymology: Also the circumstantial ad hominem: the argument is answered with an account of why the arguer wants it to be true.
committed_when: A claim has been made by someone with an obvious interest in it.
tell: The reply is entirely about who benefits, and the claim's evidence is not mentioned.
counter: Separate interest from evidence: ask what the numbers say, then ask who profits. Both questions have answers and only one is about truth.
senses: Dismissing a claim by attributing a motive to whoever made it, as though the motive settled the facts.
It works because motives are real and often relevant. But a motive explains why someone is talking, not whether what they said is accurate - and the audience conflates the two.
example: *“Of course the landlord says rents are fine - he owns the building.”* He does; the rent roll is still a document.

confused_with.tell: Appeal to motive attacks the reason behind the claim; ad hominem attacks the person's character or record.
